svg.title: Five Investment Bases, Five Cash-Yield Outcomes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-realized-cash-yield-mechanics; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Five Investment Bases, Five Cash-Yield Outcomes; subtitle: Compare realized cash divided by invested cash, not headline rates.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: All bars are independent transaction illustrations, not portfolio forecasts or components of the canonical revenue scenarios. Numeric values are realized cash-yield percentages before expenses and taxes. Certificate examples assume one year outstanding; the Texas example is one redemption event within its applicable 180-day period and is not annualized.; caption: The investment denominator matters as much as the rate. Certificate interest, auction premiums, and redeemable-deed payments follow different rules; verify the applicable statute and county settlement calculation before committing funds.; stages: label: Florida certificate at 6%; value: 6.0% cash yield on $10,000 invested; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 certificate acquired at a 6% auction rate and redeemed after one year: $600 realized interest divided by $10,000 invested. Apply Florida Statutes sections 197.432 and 197.472, including redemption-specific calculation rules.; label: Arizona certificate at 8%; value: 8.0% cash yield on $10,000 invested; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 interest-bearing certificate at an 8% bid rate for one year: $800 divided by $10,000. Arizona Revised Statutes sections 42-18114 and 42-18153 govern bid rates and redemption amounts; actual statutory month counting controls settlement.; label: New Jersey certificate at 4%; value: 4.0% interest-only yield before separate redemption charges; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 certificate bought without a premium at 4% and redeemed after one year. Interest alone contributes $400; separately analyze additional redemption amounts under N.J.S.A. 54:5-32 and 54:5-61 rather than adding them to the bid rate.; label: New Jersey premium-funded certificate; value: 2.0% interest-only yield on $20,000 committed; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Assume the same $10,000 certificate at 4% requires a separate $10,000 auction premium. Its $400 interest divided by $20,000 committed yields 2%; premium return, forfeiture, and holding rules require separate review under N.J.S.A. 54:5-33.; label: Texas nonhomestead redeemable deed; value: 25.0% event yield; no annualized comparison implied; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Assume a qualifying nonhomestead, nonagricultural property under Texas Tax Code section 34.21(e), with $10,000 total qualifying expenditure and timely redemption. A 25% premium produces $2,500; this is a statutory redemption payment, not annual interest.

text.title: Five Investment Bases, Five Cash-Yield Outcomes
text.tspan: Five Investment Bases, Five Cash-Yield Outcomes

rect.title: label: Florida certificate at 6%; value: 6.0% cash yield on $10,000 invested; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 certificate acquired at a 6% auction rate and redeemed after one year: $600 realized interest divided by $10,000 invested. Apply Florida Statutes sections 197.432 and 197.472, including redemption-specific calculation rules.

label: Arizona certificate at 8%; value: 8.0% cash yield on $10,000 invested; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 interest-bearing certificate at an 8% bid rate for one year: $800 divided by $10,000. Arizona Revised Statutes sections 42-18114 and 42-18153 govern bid rates and redemption amounts; actual statutory month counting controls settlement.

label: New Jersey certificate at 4%; value: 4.0% interest-only yield before separate redemption charges; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Assume a $10,000 certificate bought without a premium at 4% and redeemed after one year. Interest alone contributes $400; separately analyze additional redemption amounts under N.J.S.A. 54:5-32 and 54:5-61 rather than adding them to the bid rate.

label: New Jersey premium-funded certificate; value: 2.0% interest-only yield on $20,000 committed; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Assume the same $10,000 certificate at 4% requires a separate $10,000 auction premium. Its $400 interest divided by $20,000 committed yields 2%; premium return, forfeiture, and holding rules require separate review under N.J.S.A. 54:5-33.

label: Texas nonhomestead redeemable deed; value: 25.0% event yield; no annualized comparison implied; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Assume a qualifying nonhomestead, nonagricultural property under Texas Tax Code section 34.21(e), with $10,000 total qualifying expenditure and timely redemption. A 25% premium produces $2,500; this is a statutory redemption payment, not annual interest.

text.title: Assumptions: All bars are independent transaction illustrations, not portfolio forecasts or components of the canonical revenue scenarios. Numeric values are realized cash-yield percentages before expenses and taxes. Certificate examples assume one year outstanding; the Texas example is one redemption event within its applicable 180-day period and is not annualized.
